Let $A\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}$, let $f$ be holomorphic on an open
$\Omega\subseteq\mathbb C$ containing $\sigma(A)$, and let $r$ be rational
with no pole on $\Omega$. Let $\Gamma$ be an admissible Cauchy cycle for $A$
contained in $\Omega$. Write its finite chain representation as $\Gamma=\sum_\nu m_\nu\gamma_\nu$ with integer coefficients and define its coefficient-weighted length by $L_\Gamma:=\sum_\nu|m_\nu|L(\gamma_\nu)$. The integral and this length use the same signed-chain representation. Suppose
$$\sup_{z\in\Gamma}|f(z)-r(z)|\le\varepsilon,\qquad \sup_{z\in\Gamma}\|(zI-A)^{-1}\|_{\infty,\mathbb C}\le M.$$
Then
$$\|f(A)-r(A)\|_{\infty,\mathbb C} \le \frac{L_\Gamma}{2\pi}\,\varepsilon M.$$
The resolvent hypothesis may be supplied by the diskwise certificate of
[[thm-complex-resolvent-cover-certificate-soundness]]. A scalar disk error
alone does not give this matrix bound for a nonnormal matrix.

mirrors.before:
Let n,d>=1 and let f_1,...,f_n:R^d->R be continuously differentiable convex functions. Define the finite-sum objective

$$
F(x)=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x),\qquad \nabla F(x)=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\nabla f_i(x),
$$

where the gradient identity follows from [[lem-finite-sum-gradient-is-average]] and the sums use [[def-finite-sum]]. Suppose each component gradient is L-Lipschitz for a common L>0. An SVRG epoch with snapshot \tilde x and inner length m>=1 is:

1. Compute the full gradient \nabla F(\tilde x), set x_0=\tilde x.
2. For t=0,...,m-1, draw I_t uniformly from {1,...,n}, independently of the past, and set
   $$
   v_t=\nabla f_{I_t}(x_t)-\nabla f_{I_t}(\tilde x)+\nabla F(\tilde x),\qquad x_{t+1}=x_t-\eta v_t
   $$
   for a selected step size \eta>0.
3. Independently draw J uniformly from {0,...,m-1} and return x_J as the next snapshot.

The displayed procedure evaluates the snapshot component gradient at every inner update rather than caching those values. Its correction has the control-variate form of [[def-control-variate-estimator]] with coefficient one and the known finite-sum reference mean; the conditional properties needed here are proved in local results on this page. Conditional-expectation notation inherits the [[def-axiom-of-choice]] assumption from [[def-stochastic-gradient-oracle-and-unconstrained-update]].
